acceptance: `evolve worktree create --dev t --branch b` makes dev/t on branch b at origin/main (red: flag provided but not defined)
`evolve worktree cleanup --dev t` refuses a dirty tree or an unmerged branch with exit 1, and removes a merged tree together with its branch
A squash-merged PR counts as merged (a fake gh reports it merged)
fix: Add `--dev <task>` to `evolve worktree create`, with `--branch B` and base origin/main after a fetch; it places the tree under the hub's dev/ and builds the binary. Add `--dev <task>` to `evolve worktree cleanup`; it removes dev/<task> and its branch only when the tree is clean and the branch's PR is merged or its head is in origin/main. A dirty tree or an unmerged branch exits 1 naming the cause; an existing task or branch on create exits 1; git I/O exits 2. Update workspace-layout.md and runtime-reference.md.
source: console, 2026-09-30, core-function CLI inventory (operator request: a CLI request for each core function)
summary: The worktree verbs are per-cycle: `create --cycle N` and `cleanup --cycle N` (cmd_worktree.go:43-47, 64, 129). For console work, workspace-layout.md:18 has the operator run `git worktree add dev/<task> -b <branch> origin/main` and then `make -C go build` (:38). After the merge the operator removes the tree with `git worktree remove` and `git branch -D` (:36), first checking by hand that the PR merged, since git does not count a squash-merged branch as merged.
title: Console dev worktrees are created and removed with raw git; add `evolve worktree create --dev` and `evolve worktree cleanup --dev`
